title: ESP32 JTAG debugging: breakpoints and watchpoints

spans.text: JTAG lets a debugger halt real ESP32 hardware, step through source lines, and inspect variables and memory. OpenOCD bridges the target to GDB. Set a breakpoint or watchpoint on `sampleCount`; the one-second delay keeps the task from busy-spinning. JTAG pins may be unavailable or disabled on a particular board; some chips provide USB Serial/JTAG while others need an external probe.

Workflow: verify board/probe compatibility, build the ESP-IDF project with debug symbols, start OpenOCD, and attach GDB. Break at `++sampleCount` and inspect the value. For stack issues, inspect the FreeRTOS stack high-water mark; preserve logs and a core dump when diagnosing watchdog resets.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Pin assignments, probe voltage, and USB Serial/JTAG support vary by model. Debug only boards you own or are authorized to use. Do not weaken JTAG, secure-boot, or flash-encryption policy on production devices; eFuse changes may be irreversible.
